title: SecB MCP Upstream Registry Schema
description: Declaration of upstream MCP servers SecB may front. Declares WHAT an upstream is and WHERE it must run, never how to spawn it: spawn-plan resolution is a pure downstream projection and activation remains a separate operator-authorized step.

wsl_distro.description: Distro name used to build the wsl.exe bridge when a wsl-runtime upstream is resolved from a Windows host.

id.description: Stable identifier. Also the namespace prefix once tools are fronted, so it must not collide across upstreams.

runtime.description: Where this upstream must actually execute or listen. 'any' means the command resolves on either host without a bridge.

timeout_ms.description: Per-request timeout for this upstream. Omitted means the proxy default.

max_concurrency.description: Cap on in-flight calls to this upstream. Omitted means the proxy default, which follows the gateway-core house limit of 4.

tools_allow.description: If present, ONLY these upstream tool names are fronted. Exposure is otherwise all-or-nothing per upstream, which is what forces a large merged listing. An absent list means every tool; an empty list means none, and is a deliberate way to declare an upstream without exposing it.

tools_deny.description: Upstream tool names never fronted. Applied after tools_allow, so deny wins on overlap.

max_response_bytes.description: Cap on one upstream response, measured after serialisation. An upstream reply is foreign text entering a model context, so an unbounded reply is a context-flooding surface, not just a memory concern.

verified_status.description: Last recorded observation. Advisory provenance only; it never grants or withholds reachability at resolve time.
